newsitem.title: BOSNIA: New Bosnian Federation parliament approves flag. [corrected 23:15 gmt]
newsitem.headline: New Bosnian Federation parliament approves flag. [corrected 23:15 gmt]

text.p: Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation parliament held its inaugural session on Wednesday, almost two months after postwar elections, and adopted a bi-national flag, coat-of-arms and seal.

But it did not address the first substantive issue on its agenda as international peace coordinators had hoped -- namely, the appointment of a new government for the Federation entity comprising half of Bosnia.

Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic had said the parliament would approve a cabinet this week and at the same time remove a senior defence official from the wartime Federation government to comply with U.S. conditions for military aid.

Washington has demanded the sacking of deputy defence minister Hasan Cengic, a Moslem nationalist with links to Iran, before it delivers $100 million in arms to help the Federation reach military parity with Bosnia's Serb Republic.
It was not immediately known when the 204-member Federation legislature would convene next.

Bosnia's citizens voted on September 14 for joint governing institutions to reunite a country split by war into ethnic fiefs. But efforts to establish the complex ruling structure have been slowed by nationalist feuding and manoeuvring.

A Serb-Moslem-Croat presidency and House of Representatives is to preside over a union of autonomous Moslem-Croat and Serb entities, with separate parliaments, under terms of the 1995 Dayton peace treaty.

The tripartite executive branch began meeting only in late October after session venues were agreed and the Serb nationalist member dropped his refusal to sign an oath of loyalty to a single state of Bosnia.

The House of Representatives has yet to convene. Session venues remain in dispute, revolving around Serb resistance to meetings in Sarajevo where they fear violence in retaliation for their long, bloody siege of the capital.

The Serb Republic assembly has met once, in the northern city of Banja Luka. But minority Moslem deputies elected by refugees expelled during the war walked out to avoid having to swear a Christian Orthodox oath of office.
In Sarajevo on Wednesday, the Federation parliament overwhelmingly approved a new flag, coat of arms and official seal which combine Bosnian Moslem and Croat national symbols.

The flag bears a crest split into three sections -- the green Moslem lily, the red-and-white Croat checkerboard, and a circle of white stars on a blue backdrop that represent the federation's 10 cantons but also evoke aspirations to European Union membership someday. (Corrects symbolic meaning of circle of stars.)

Izetbegovic's Moslem nationalist SDA party has 105 of the parliament's 204 seats, the Bosnia wing of Croatia's ruling nationalist HDZ party 66, a Moslem-led moderate party and a civic coalition 14 each, with the rest held by fringe groups.
